title: Paid orders
sql: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE status='paid' ORDER BY id;
explanation: Filter rows before aggregation.

title: Missing amount
sql: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE amount IS NULL;
explanation: Use IS NULL, not equality.

title: Count rows and known amounts
sql: SELECT COUNT(*),COUNT(amount) FROM orders;
explanation: Missing and zero are different.

title: Paid total
sql: SELECT SUM(amount) FROM orders WHERE status='paid';
explanation: The sum is at order grain.

title: Customers with multiple orders
sql: SELECT customer_id FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*)>1 ORDER BY customer_id;
explanation: HAVING filters groups.

title: Amounts above100
sql: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE amount>100 ORDER BY id;
explanation: Strict greater-than excludes equal100.

title: Conditional paid totals
sql: SELECT customer_id,SUM(CASE WHEN status='paid' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY customer_id;
explanation: The CASE defines eligible contribution.

title: Customers without any orders
sql: SELECT c.id FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id=c.id) ORDER BY c.id;
explanation: An anti-match does not require duplicated join rows.

title: Retain customers with zero paid orders
sql: SELECT c.id,COUNT(o.id) FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id=c.id AND o.status='paid' GROUP BY c.id ORDER BY c.id;
explanation: The right-side filter belongs in ON to preserve unmatched customers.

title: Latest order per customer
sql: WITH r AS(SELECT id,customer_id,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY day DESC,id DESC) rn FROM orders) SELECT customer_id,id FROM r WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY customer_id;
explanation: Timestamp and ID define the winner.

title: Second distinct nonmissing amount
sql: SELECT DISTINCT amount FROM orders WHERE amount IS NOT NULL ORDER BY amount DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1;
explanation: DISTINCT makes the rank semantic explicit; absent second values return no row.

title: Running paid total
sql: SELECT id,SUM(amount) OVER(ORDER BY day,id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) FROM orders WHERE status='paid' ORDER BY day,id;
explanation: Explicit frame and unique ordering define accumulation.

title: Previous paid amount
sql: SELECT id,LAG(amount) OVER(PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY day,id) FROM orders WHERE status='paid' ORDER BY customer_id,day,id;
explanation: WHERE limits the window input to paid orders.

title: Customer paid-share of total
sql: WITH a AS(SELECT customer_id,SUM(amount) total FROM orders WHERE status='paid' GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT customer_id,ROUND(1.0*total/SUM(total) OVER(),4) FROM a ORDER BY customer_id;
explanation: Convert to noninteger arithmetic and state rounding.

title: Date totals
sql: SELECT day,SUM(amount) FROM orders WHERE status='paid' GROUP BY day ORDER BY day;
explanation: These ISO dates sort lexically here; production date types/dialects need explicit treatment.

title: Rank tied amounts
sql: SELECT id,RANK() OVER(ORDER BY amount DESC),DENSE_RANK() OVER(ORDER BY amount DESC) FROM orders WHERE amount IS NOT NULL ORDER BY amount DESC,id;
explanation: RANK leaves a gap after the two100amounts.

title: Above customer average
sql: SELECT o.id FROM orders o WHERE amount>(SELECT AVG(i.amount) FROM orders i WHERE i.customer_id=o.customer_id) ORDER BY o.id;
explanation: AVG ignores missing values; a customer with one known amount has no above-average order.

title: Distinct paying customers
sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM orders WHERE status='paid';
explanation: Four paid orders do not mean four paying customers.

title: Verify missing and zero separately
sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN amount IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),SUM(CASE WHEN amount=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM orders;
explanation: Unknown amount is not known zero.

title: Paid amount with last-order annotation
sql: SELECT id,amount,MAX(day) OVER(PARTITION BY customer_id) FROM orders WHERE status='paid' ORDER BY id;
explanation: The date annotation does not imply each row is the latest; use row filtering when that is the question.
